unity-catalog-oss:rest-spec-support:curr.notes: Exposes an Iceberg REST endpoint (/api/2.1/unity-catalog/iceberg) that serves Delta UniForm tables to Iceberg clients such as Trino and DuckDB.
caveats: Read-oriented: tables can't be created or committed through the IRC endpoint
Only Delta tables with UniForm enabled are visible to Iceberg clients

unity-catalog-oss:v2-spec-support:curren.notes: UniForm generates format v2 Iceberg metadata for Delta tables served over the REST endpoint.
caveats: UniForm requires deletion vectors to be disabled on the Delta side, so the generated v2 metadata never carries delete files

unity-catalog-oss:v3-spec-support:curren.notes: No format v3 support announced for the OSS server; UniForm metadata generation targets format v2.

unity-catalog-oss:managed-offering:curre.notes: Self-hosted OSS project; the managed Unity is a different, proprietary product.

unity-catalog-oss:serves-own-irc:current.notes: The IRC path is a secondary, read-leaning surface (Delta UniForm read-as-Iceberg) rather than full table lifecycle, and it vends no credentials: the documented read example authenticates with token 'not_used' and the engine supplies its own storage keys. Held to the same read+write-with-vended-credentials bar as every catalog, it does not qualify.

unity-catalog-oss:rw-foreign-irc:current.notes: No bundled query engine, so the catalog cannot itself read or write foreign tables over IRC: foreign-table access needs separate compute.
caveats: The source rubric scores 'no engine' as 0 (BYO compute), so this is recorded as not supported rather than unknown

unity-catalog-oss:federation-broker:curr.notes: No catalog-of-catalogs brokering in the OSS edition.

unity-catalog-oss:multi-engine-multi-clo.notes: Mostly Spark, DuckDB and Daft via the UC-native API; not broad IRC.

unity-catalog-oss:governance-cred-vendin.notes: Coarse object grants exist but authorization is off by default; no named-role RBAC, row/column masks or ABAC (all marked unplanned on the roadmap), and credential vending is static pre-configured keys rather than short-lived STS-style vending.
